居間にいる藤ねえから離れて、縁側で夕方の続きをする。
昼間から散々こじれた作戦会議だから、そう簡単に決着はつくまい、と気合いをいれて会合に臨んだのだが、

pages.en:
We leave Fuji in the sitting room and resume our earlier conversation on the veranda.

The strategy meeting had been hopelessly tangled since this afternoon, so I came prepared for a long struggle. Instead—
pages.mirrorMoon:
We get away from Fuji-nee, who’s in the living room, and continue the meeting out on the porch.
I expected it not to finish so easily because we’ve talked so much since noon, but…

pages.ja:
「柳洞寺に挑むのは現段階では無理よ。
こっちで罠をしかけて、キャスターをおびき出すしかないでしょ」
と、遠坂は実にすっぱり結論を出した。

「柳洞寺に挑むのは現段階では無理よ。

pages.en:
“Attacking Ryuudou Temple is impossible at present.

“We'll have to set a trap on our own ground and draw Caster out.”

Tohsaka delivers her conclusion with remarkable finality.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“It’s impossible to challenge the Ryuudou Temple at the moment.
The only thing we can do is to set up some sort of trap to lure Caster out.”
Tohsaka concludes.

pages.ja:
「
いや。それは、その通りなんだが」
「問題は罠をどうするかだけど。
……ま、二三心当たりがあるから衛宮くんは待機していて。最悪、貴方とセイバーにはエサになってもらうから」
pages.jaRuby:
「
いや。それは、その通りなんだが」
「問題は罠をどうするかだけど。
……ま、二三心当たりがあるから衛宮くんは待機していて。最悪、貴方とセイバーにはエサになってもらうから」
pages.en:
“—Well. Yes, that's true, but…”

“The only question is what sort of trap to use.

“…I have two or three possibilities in mind, so stand by for now. At worst, you and Saber can serve as bait.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Well. You’re… right, but…”
“The problem is the trap.
…Well, I have two or three possible ideas, so you can stand by for now. In the worst case, I’ll have you and Saber be the bait.”

pages.ja:
物騒な事を言って、遠坂は雨戸を開けた。
冷えた空気が内部に侵入してくる。
それでもこの縁側は特別なのか、肌寒い程度で留まっている。
……五年前の夜と同じ。
この縁側だけは、冬でも月見ができるぐらい温かい。

pages.en:
Having made that ominous pronouncement, Tohsaka opens the storm shutters.

Cold air spills inside.

Perhaps there is something special about this veranda, however, for the chill never becomes unbearable.

…Just as on that night five years ago.

This veranda alone remains warm enough for moon-gazing even in winter.
pages.mirrorMoon:
After saying something dangerous, Tohsaka opens the sliding door.
The cold air comes in.
Maybe this porch is special, as it’s only a bit chilly.
…It’s just like that night five years ago.
This porch is warm enough to be able to sit down and watch the moon even during wintertime.

pages.ja:
「
いい結界ね。わたしの家とは違って、人間の情を感じる」
縁側に腰をかけ、ぼんやりと庭を見つめながら、遠坂はそんなコトを呟いた。
「ちょっと付き合わない？ なんでもない話があるんだけど」
pages.jaRuby:
「
いい結界ね。わたしの家とは違って、人間の情を感じる」
縁側に腰をかけ、ぼんやりと庭を見つめながら、遠坂はそんなコトを呟いた。
「ちょっと付き合わない？ なんでもない話があるんだけど」
pages.en:
“—This is a lovely bounded field. Unlike my house, it possesses a human warmth.”

Tohsaka sits on the edge of the veranda and murmurs the words while gazing absently into the garden.

“Will you keep me company? There's something unimportant I'd like to talk about.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“It’s a good boundary field. I feel some human emotion, unlike the one at my place.”
Tohsaka murmurs while sitting at the porch, staring into the yard.
“Do you want to sit here with me? I just want to talk.”

pages.ja:
「
」
無言で隣に座る。
話がある、だなんて言っておいて、遠坂は一向に喋らない。
仕方がないので、ぼんやりと庭を眺めた。
pages.jaRuby:
「
」
無言で隣に座る。
話がある、だなんて言っておいて、遠坂は一向に喋らない。
仕方がないので、ぼんやりと庭を眺めた。
pages.en:
“——”

I sit beside her without a word.

Despite claiming she wished to talk, Tohsaka says nothing at all.

With no other choice, I stare vaguely into the garden.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“”
I sit next to her silently.
She said she wants to talk, but she doesn’t say anything.
I can’t do anything else, so I stare at the yard absent-mindedly.

pages.ja:
「
」
月は見えない。
吐く息が白いのは、やはり雪が降ったからだろう。
ふと横を見ると、遠坂も白い息をこぼしながら庭を見つめていた。
pages.jaRuby:

」

pages.en:
“——”

The moon is hidden.

Our breath turns white, perhaps because of the snow.

When I glance aside, Tohsaka too is watching the garden as pale breath spills from her lips.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“”
I can’t see the moon.
My breath is white, probably because it snowed earlier.
When I look to my side, Tohsaka is staring at the yard with white breath as well.

pages.ja:
「
」
少し体をずらせば、きっと肩が触れる距離。
それに動揺する事はなかった。
単に慣れたのか、冬の夜のおかげなのか。
こんなに近くに遠坂がいるのに、不思議と気持ちは落ち着いている。

pages.en:
“——”

If I shifted only slightly, our shoulders would surely touch.

The thought does not disturb me.

Perhaps I have grown accustomed to her. Perhaps it is the winter night.

Though Tohsaka sits so close, I feel strangely at peace.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“”
I can touch her shoulder if I move a bit.
I’m not disturbed by that fact.
Is it because I’m getting used to it or because of the winter night?
Tohsaka is so close to me, but I feel so calm.

pages.ja:
「
で。話ってなんだよ、遠坂」
なんとなく聞かれたがってるな、と感じて話しかけた。
pages.jaRuby:
「
で。話ってなんだよ、遠坂」
なんとなく聞かれたがってるな、と感じて話しかけた。
pages.en:
“—So? What did you want to talk about, Tohsaka?”

I have the sense that she is waiting to be asked, so I oblige her.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“So, what do you want to talk about, Tohsaka?”
I ask her, feeling that she’s waiting for that question.

pages.ja: 「……ん。ちょっとね、このうちって特殊だから。人のふり見て我がふり直せじゃないけど。その、衛宮くんはそのままでもいいのかなって、ふと思った」
pages.jaRuby: 「……ん。ちょっとね、このうちって特殊だから。人のふり見て我がふり直せじゃないけど。その、衛宮くんはそのままでもいいのかなって、ふと思った」
pages.en: “…Mm. It's just that this house is unusual. I suppose seeing someone else's behavior made me reconsider my own. It occurred to me that perhaps you might be fine as you are, Emiya.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “…Hm. Well, this place is a bit special. I just thought that you might be fine as you are right now.”

pages.ja:
「うわ。そのままでいいって、半人前でいいって事かよ」
「そうじゃないんだけど、そうなのかもね。
衛宮切嗣って人がどんな魔術師だったか知らないけど、この屋敷はすごく自然なのよ。魔術師の工房のくせに開けてる。
四方の門は開け放たれていて、入るのも帰るのもご自由にって感じ。きっと守るべき知識がないから、何物にも縛られないのよ」

四方の門は開け放たれていて、入るのも帰るのもご自由にって感じ。きっと守るべき[ruby text=もの o2o=1]知識がないから、何物にも縛られないのよ」
pages.en:
“Wow. Fine as I am? You mean I should remain half-trained forever?”

“That isn't what I mean. Though perhaps it is, in a way.

“I don't know what sort of mage Kiritsugu Emiya was, but this estate feels extraordinarily natural. Though it is a mage's workshop, it lies open.

“Every gate in every direction stands unbarred, as though anyone may enter or leave as they please. There must be nothing here—no secret knowledge—that needs protecting, and so the house is bound by nothing.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Whoa. Do you mean I’m good enough as an amateur?”
“Not exactly, but maybe so.
I don’t know what kind of a magus Emiya Kiritsugu was, but this place is really natural. It’s very open even though this is the workshop of a magus.
All the doors are open, free for anyone to come in and leave. It’s probably not bounded by anything because there’s no knowledge here to protect.”

pages.ja: 「貴方のお父さんが魔術師じゃなくて魔術使いになれって言ったのはそういう事なんだと思う。なんにもないかわりに、何処へだって行けるんだから」
pages.jaRuby: 「貴方のお父さんが魔術師じゃなくて魔術使いになれって言ったのはそういう事なんだと思う。なんにもないかわりに、何処へだって行けるんだから」
pages.en: “I think that is why your father told you to become a spellcaster rather than a mage. You may possess nothing, but in exchange, you are free to go anywhere.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “I think that’s what your dad meant by telling you to become a magic user and not a magus. You have nothing, but in its place, you can go anywhere.”

pages.ja:
「なんだ。遠坂はそうじゃないのか」
「ええ、わたしの家は違う。近所じゃ幽霊屋敷って言われてるけど、事実その通りなのよね。来るものは拒む、そのくせ入ってきたものは逃がさない」
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“What? Isn't your house the same?”

“No. Mine is different. People in the neighborhood call it a haunted mansion, and they're entirely correct. It refuses anything that comes near, yet never releases what manages to enter.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“What? You’re not like that?”
“No, my place is different. My mansion is called a haunted house, and it really is. It rejects anybody that comes, yet it doesn’t release anyone that comes in.”

pages.ja:
「……時々ね、なんか違うなって思うんだけど、これが変えられないのよ。
呪われてるとかそういうんじゃなくて、わたし自身そういう在り方が気に入っちゃってるわけ。こういう性格をしてるから後継者に選ばれたんでしょうけど、気が付いた時にはわりとショックだった」
pages.jaRuby:
「……時々ね、なんか違うなって思うんだけど、これが変えられないのよ。

pages.en:
“…Sometimes I think that isn't quite right. But I can't change it.

“It isn't that I'm cursed. I simply happen to like being that way. I was probably chosen as successor because I was born with this personality, but realizing it still came as a considerable shock.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…I sometimes think it’s wrong, but it’s not something I can change.
It’s not like it’s cursed, but it’s just that I like how it is. I was chosen as the successor probably because of my personality. But it was pretty shocking when I realized it.”

pages.ja:
「
ふむ。それはつまり、自分がいじめっこだと気が付いた時か？」
「…………思うんだけど。衛宮くんって、歯に衣きせない質よね」
「そうか？ 遠坂を見習って回りくどく言ったつもりなんだが」
「……まったく。そういうところが直球だって言ってるの」

pages.en:
“—Hmm. You mean the moment you realized you were a bully?”

“…………You know, Emiya, you really are incapable of softening your words.”

“Am I? I thought I was taking after you and putting it indirectly.”

“…Honestly. That is exactly what makes you so painfully direct.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Hm. Is that when you realized that you’re a bully?”
“……You’re not one to mince words, huh?”
“Really? I thought I was being indirect, just like you.”
“…Geez. I’m telling you that’s direct.”

pages.ja:
はあ、と大きく息を吐いてうなだれる。
吐息の残滓は白く、冷たい夜にゆっくりと溶けていった。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
She exhales deeply and lets her head fall.

The white remnant of her breath dissolves slowly into the frigid night.
pages.mirrorMoon:
She sighs and hangs her head.
Her sigh is white and slowly melts into the cold night.

pages.ja:
……その横顔を盗み見て、思い出した。
赤い校舎。
ライダーによって倒れ伏した生徒たちを見て、遠坂は何も言わなかった。
いつも通り気丈に振る舞いながら、唇を噛んで、膝を小さく震わせていた。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
…I steal a glance at her profile and remember.

The school stained red.

When Tohsaka saw the students Rider had struck down, she said nothing.

She held herself as proudly as ever, even as she bit her lip and her knees trembled faintly.
pages.mirrorMoon:
…Seeing her face makes me remember…
The red school.
Tohsaka didn’t say anything when she saw the unconscious students.
In spite of her shaking knees, she bit her lip and acted firm as usual.

pages.ja:
……その時に気づいたのだ。
魔術師として完璧になればなるほど、こいつは、遠坂凛っていう自分を殺しているのではないかと。
pages.jaRuby:
……その時に気づいたのだ。
魔術師として完璧になればなるほど、こいつは、遠坂凛っていう自分を殺しているのではないかと。
pages.en:
…That was when the thought first came to me.

The closer she comes to perfection as a mage, the more she may be killing the person called Rin Tohsaka.
pages.mirrorMoon:
…I realized at that time.
That she might be killing her true self by acting like a perfect magus.

pages.ja:
「遠坂は、きつかったのか」
不安になって訊いた。
pages.jaRuby:
「遠坂は、きつかったのか」
不安になって訊いた。
pages.en:
“Tohsaka… was it hard for you?”

The question escapes me in sudden unease.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Was it hard for you, Tohsaka?”
I get uneasy, so I ask.

pages.ja:
「魔術の修行が？ おあいにくさま、苦しいなんて思ったコトはなかったわ。大抵の事はすんなりこなせたし、出来なくて挫折した事なんてなかったしね。
それに新しい事を覚えるのは楽しかった。さっきも言ったでしょ？ わたし、生まれつきそういう性格なんだって。だから衛宮くんの心配は杞憂ってヤツよ」
pages.jaRuby:
「魔術の修行が？ おあいにくさま、苦しいなんて思ったコトはなかったわ。大抵の事はすんなりこなせたし、出来なくて挫折した事なんてなかったしね。
それに新しい事を覚えるのは楽しかった。さっきも言ったでしょ？ わたし、生まれつきそういう性格なんだって。だから衛宮くんの心配は杞憂ってヤツよ」
pages.en:
“Training in magecraft? Sorry to disappoint you, but I never once found it painful. Most things came easily, and I never failed so badly that I despaired.

“Besides, learning new things was fun. I told you, didn't I? I was born this way. So all this concern of yours is completely misplaced.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“You mean the training? Sorry, but I never thought it was hard. I was able to do most things without a problem, and I was never discouraged because I couldn’t do something.
And it was fun for me to learn new things. I told you, right? I was born with this personality. So there’s no need for you to worry.”

pages.ja:
あっさりと言う。
そこには強がりも偽りもなく、遠坂は本当に気持ちのいい笑みを浮かべていた。
pages.jaRuby:
あっさりと言う。
そこには強がりも偽りもなく、遠坂は本当に気持ちのいい笑みを浮かべていた。
pages.en:
She says it without hesitation.

There is neither bravado nor deception in her. Tohsaka's smile is one of genuine, effortless happiness.
pages.mirrorMoon:
She simply says so.
There’s no bluff nor lie in her statement, and Tohsaka is smiling.

pages.ja: 「そっか。なら学校はどうなんだ？ 魔術師としてやっていくんなら、学校に行っても無意味なんじゃないか？」
pages.jaRuby: 「そっか。なら学校はどうなんだ？ 魔術師としてやっていくんなら、学校に行っても無意味なんじゃないか？」
pages.en: “I see. Then what about school? If you're going to live as a mage, isn't attending school pointless?”
pages.mirrorMoon: “I see. Then what about school? If you’re going to live as a magus, isn’t it meaningless to go to school?”

pages.ja:
「無意味とまではいかないけど寄り道でしょうね。
けど無駄じゃないわよ？ 学生って楽しいもの。わたしね、基本的に快楽主義者なの。父さんの跡を継ぐのは義務だけど、それだって自分が楽しくなければやらないわ。
マスターになったのだって自分の力を試したいからだし、衛宮くんと協力してるのだって、貴方が面白いからだし」
pages.jaRuby:
「無意味とまではいかないけど寄り道でしょうね。

マスターになったのだって自分の力を試したいからだし、衛宮くんと協力してるのだって、貴方が面白いからだし」
pages.en:
“I wouldn't call it pointless, but it is certainly a detour.

“It isn't a waste, though. Being a student is fun. At heart, I'm a hedonist. Inheriting my father's work is my duty, but even that isn't something I would do if I couldn't enjoy it.

“I became a Master because I wanted to test my power. And I'm working with you because I find you interesting, Emiya.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“It’s not meaningless, but it is straying away from my path.
But it’s not pointless. Being a student is fun. I’m up for anything fun. It’s a duty to succeed my dad, but I wouldn’t do it if it wasn’t fun.
I became a Master because I wanted to test my powers, and I’m cooperating with you because you’re funny.”

pages.ja:
「
」
俺が面白い、という意見はさておくとして、それで胸のつかえはなくなってくれた。
pages.jaRuby:
「
」
俺が面白い、という意見はさておくとして、それで胸のつかえはなくなってくれた。
pages.en:
“——”

Setting aside her opinion that I am interesting, the weight in my chest is gone.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“”
Ignoring the comment that I’m funny, my worries disappear.

pages.ja:
魔術師の家系。
重い歴史と血脈に縛られた遠坂は、暗い影を背負っていると思っていた。
けれどそんなのはこっちの思いこみだ。
こいつにとっては“遠坂家”は重い影でもなんでもなくて、遠坂凛は自由に、自分のやりたいようにやってきたんだから。

けれどそんなのはこっちの思いこみだ。

pages.en:
A family of magi.

I imagined Tohsaka burdened by a dark shadow, chained to the weight of history and blood.

But that was only my assumption.

To her, the Tohsaka family is no burden at all. Rin Tohsaka has always lived freely, doing exactly as she wished.
pages.mirrorMoon:
A family of magi.
I thought Tohsaka was carrying a dark shadow because she’s bound by a heavy history and bloodline.
But that was just my prejudice.
The “Tohsaka family” is not a burden on her, and she’s done what she wanted up to now.

「ありがと。で、もちろんそういう衛宮くんも楽しかったんでしょ？ そうでもなければ魔術の修行なんて続かないものね」
当然のように遠坂は言う。
が、それは、

pages.en:
“Oh, perfect timing. I'll use the guest room on the right.”

I watch her go in a stupor, then look into the mirror in the hall.

“——”

My face is as red as an apple.

…Damn it.

I don't care how far apart the rooms are. What is she thinking, sleeping in the same house as me?
